messages:
nina shah: DeployBot alerted on v3.4.5 canary in eu-central. 5xxs up to 3.1% on /v1/generate. DeployBot suggests auto-rollback to v3.4.4.
deploy-bot: DeployBot: Canary breach detected for release v3.4.5. error-rate > 2% on /v1/generate (eu-central). Recommend auto-rollback to v3.4.4. reason: post-deploy-cache-exhaust
oliver grant: Hold auto-rollback. v3.4.5 shipped a cache serialization change and a small DB index migration. Rolling back the binary without reversing the format will leave live caches and queued jobs incompatible. We should avoid a blunt global revert.
rachel wong: +1. We can do a regional rollback for eu-central to protect customers there, while the rest of fleet stays on v3.4.5. That buys time for a migration fix or a compatibility shim.
nina shah: Ops plan proposal: 1) cancel auto-rollback via operator override 2) pin eu-central traffic for dedicated/hosted to v3.4.4 (100%) 3) run migration-fix and cache rehydrate in eu-central; if fix fails in 20m then execute manual rollback with DB reverse steps and customer comms.
ops-bot: Note: DeployBot auto-rollback timer is scheduled in 4m. Operator override required to cancel.
rachel wong: Ops pin command (example):
```bash
routectl set-weight --route api-eu-central --version v3.4.4 --weight 100 --match-header "X-Env: hosted,dedicated"
```
This pins hosted/dedicated traffic in eu-central to v3.4.4 while leaving private clusters untouched.
oliver grant: Migration-fix snippet (idempotent):
```bash
psql -h pg-eu-1 -c "DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_indexes WHERE indexname='idx_msg_ts_v345') THEN CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_msg_ts_v345 ON messages (created_at); END IF; END$$;"
```
nina shah: I'll apply operator override to cancel auto-rollback and run the pin. @rachel please prepare the short customer note; ops to validate synthetic checks after fix.
ops-bot: Operator override applied by nina shah. Auto-rollback cancelled.
rachel wong: Customer note draft: "We observed increased 5xx errors in eu-central after today's release. We pinned traffic for eu-central to the prior stable release to protect ongoing workloads and are applying a targeted fix. We'll update in 30 minutes with monitoring results." Keep it brief.
oliver grant: Running migration-fix now on replicas in eu-central (shard-a & shard-b). Also preparing a compatibility shim that will try new deserialize then fall back to legacy if it fails; can push as v3.4.5-shim if needed.
rachel wong: Ops confirm pin applied. Traffic counters show hosted/dedicated in eu-central now at v3.4.4 = 100%. Test slice: v3.4.5-shim on 3% internal test traffic.
ops-bot: Canary for v3.4.5-shim shows error-rate 0.2% on test-slice.
nina shah: Validation: migration script completed on shard-a and shard-b. Synthetic checks show 0 errors, p95 latency stable. Ready to re-open eu-central to v3.4.5-shim in a controlled ramp.
oliver grant: Let's ramp to 10% for 10 minutes, validate, then 50%, then full. If errors exceed 1% at any step revert back to pinned v3.4.4 and execute manual rollback runbook.
rachel wong: Ramped to 10% -> metrics good. 50% -> metrics good. Rolling to 100% on v3.4.5-shim now.
deploy-bot: DeployBot: Canary metrics restored for v3.4.5-shim in eu-central. Auto-rollback remains cancelled by operator.
oncall-bot: Incident logged: INC-2117, severity: P2, region: eu-central, mitigation: regional pin + migration-fix + compatibility shim; follow-up: postmortem + release-note addendum assigned (rachel wong).
nina shah: Decision: no global rollback. We applied regional pin, ran a compatibility fix, validated via staged ramp, and restored traffic. Action items: - oliver: open PR for pre-deploy cache/migration checks - rachel: update release notes and customer comms - ops: add regional pin runbook entry. Closing thread when postmortem link posted.
